wording: In a 200-speaker copying toy, majority-amplifying copying (c 1.5, a stand-in for Trudgill's majority rule) eliminated a variant starting at 15% (P89's Irish share in 1871) or 30% in every run within about 3-5 generations, and selection b 0.3 for the variant did not rescue it (fixation 0 from 15%, 0.019 from 30%; both pre-registered rescue checks not supported); under neutral copying a 15% variant fixed in 15.4% of runs. In this toy a minority rise such as Liverpool's needs either much stronger selection or a copying rule without majority amplification.
